hypotheses.claim: Rust FFI boundary has negligible invocation overhead (< 5ns per call)
hypotheses.causal_mechanism: Direct extern C ABI pointer passing compiles to standard assembly call instruction without marshalling penalty.
limitations: Not yet benchmarked on Cortex-M bare-metal

failed_approaches.approach_name: Dynamic Marshalling via JSON-RPC String Passing over FFI
failed_approaches.cause_of_death: JSON serialization and heap string allocation overhead (1.8µs) completely dominated the 40ns native execution payload.
failed_approaches.scope_condition: High-frequency in-process C-ABI / FFI calls (>= 10,000 calls/sec)

assumptions.statement: Host CPU supports AVX2 SIMD instructions natively without emulation

contradictions.description: Lockless SPSC queue achieved 20M ops/s on x86_64, but suffered memory ordering race on ARM64 Cortex-A72 without explicit acquire-release fence

decisions.rationale: Direct string passing over FFI failed due to allocation overhead; pivot to zero-copy pinned Memory<T> / Span<T> pointer sharing.
